If I could make one change to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would disable the new downward swipe gesture to summon Siri AI. There are already plenty of ways to invoke Siri without breaking my muscle memory for opening Notification Center on my iPhone and iPad.

Meanwhile, on the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even into late August, new test builds keep adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one change I'd love to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate Makes MacBook Battery Percentage Harder to Read

macOS 27 Golden Gate includes a redesigned menu bar battery control. By default, the percentage doesn't show — just a battery-shaped visual indicator icon.

In that state, it looks fine. I also keep the percentage turned off on my iPhone, which has the same kind of battery indicator. But on the Mac, I've always leaned toward showing the percentage.

If you turn on "Show Percentage" in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it puts the number inside the battery icon. I assume this is to keep things consistent with how iOS 27 does it on the iPhone.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon on the iPhone was a dense packing solution to free up space next to the notch or Dynamic Island. As for the Mac, the lack of screen space issue doesn't really exist for me — even in the menu bar.

I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on my 15" MacBook Air since the first developer beta dropped on day one. I've found that I pay less attention to my battery percentage in general, because it's harder for my eyes to pick out.

I'm hoping Apple will reconsider this design decision down the road, especially if it bothers more users. In the meantime, I've at least solved the problem for myself.

I used Codex to put together a simple menu bar utility that shows the current battery status and percentage clearly and reliably, with the visual clarity I'd expect. If you think it might help you too, you can download and install it for free here.
